Summary: Mark's Gospel is the shortest and fastest-moving — a breathless account of Jesus' ministry that asks one question from start to finish: who is this man? Action follows action, and the disciples keep misunderstanding, until a Roman soldier at the cross finally sees. This guide follows Mark's pace, so you can feel the urgency and answer the question for yourself.
Steps: Read Mark in a few sittings, noticing the word "immediately" and the speed of the story; Track the question of Jesus' identity: what do the demons, the crowds, the disciples, and Jesus himself say about him?; Study the three passion predictions (Mark 8:31, 9:31, 10:33-34) and the disciples' reactions to each; Follow Peter through the Gospel, from his confession to his denial, and ask what discipleship costs; Read the cross and resurrection account (Mark 14-16) slowly, after the fast pace of the rest; End by answering, in your own words, the question Jesus asks in Mark 8:29: "Who do you say I am?"
Questions: Why does Mark move so fast — and what does that speed do to the way you read about Jesus?; Why do the disciples misunderstand Jesus so often, and where do you misunderstand him the same way?; What does Mark's emphasis on suffering say about what following Jesus actually involves?; Why does Mark end the way he does — and what response does that ending demand?; If someone asked you who Jesus is, based only on Mark, what would you say?
Application: Tell one person this week, in your own words, who Jesus is according to Mark — not a rehearsed answer, but the one you actually believe.
